sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Oprah Winfrey's hair is an amazing and ever-changing object of design.
sentences.zh: 奥普拉·温弗瑞的发型是一个令人惊叹且不断演变的设计对象。

sentences.en: A quick Google image search of her and you can see it in a dozen different styles.
sentences.zh: 在谷歌上快速搜索她的图片，你就能看到她尝试过十几种不同的风格。

sentences.en: But there's a consistency too.
sentences.zh: 但其中也有一种连贯性。

sentences.en: A brand.
sentences.zh: 一种品牌感。

sentences.en: A familiarity.
sentences.zh: 一种熟悉感。

sentences.en: Like if you took Oprah's face out of all those Google images
sentences.zh: 就像如果你把奥普拉的脸从那些谷歌图片中移走，

sentences.en: so that all you could see was a series of pictures of hair, you'd still know it was her.
sentences.zh: 只留下一系列头发的照片，你依然能认出那是她。

sentences.en: And even though she's done weaves and braids and all sorts of styles,
sentences.zh: 尽管她尝试过编织、辫子和各种各样的造型，

sentences.en: she's also a natural, meaning she doesn't use chemical relaxers to try to straighten her hair.
sentences.zh: 她也一直保持自然发质，这意味着她不使用化学柔顺剂来拉直头发。

sentences.en: And that's actually something Oprah and I have in common.
sentences.zh: 这其实也是我和奥普拉的共同点。

sentences.en: That's producer Leela Day from the Stute Podcast,
sentences.zh: 说话的是来自《Stute》播客的制作人莉拉·戴，

sentences.en: which is about stories from across the Black diaspora.
sentences.zh: 该播客讲述的是黑人侨民的故事。

sentences.en: And since I'm a white guy with very little hair,
sentences.zh: 既然我是一个头发稀疏的白人男性，

sentences.en: I'm actually going to hand this one entirely over to her now.
sentences.zh: 我现在要把这一期节目完全交给她来主持。

sentences.en: Oprah gives most of the credit for her amazing natural hair to one person.
sentences.zh: 奥普拉将她那令人惊叹的自然发质的大部分功劳归功于一个人。

sentences.en: This is Andre Walker who's done my hair for 18 years.
sentences.zh: 这位是安德烈·沃克，他为我打理头发已经18年了。

sentences.en: And I've been through some really good styles.
sentences.zh: 我经历过一些非常棒的造型。

sentences.en: And a couple of bad years.
sentences.zh: 也经历过几年糟糕的时期。

sentences.en: But right now we're doing the most part.
sentences.zh: 但目前我们做得非常出色。

sentences.en: They've been really exceptional.
sentences.zh: 它们真的非常特别。

sentences.en: They've been really good.
sentences.zh: 它们真的很棒。

sentences.en: You've done an amazing job.
sentences.zh: 你做得太棒了。

sentences.en: That's a very difficult thing to do.
sentences.zh: 这是一件非常困难的事情。

sentences.en: That's why you need the same person who knows your hair doing it all the time as well.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么你需要一个了解你发质的人一直为你打理。

sentences.en: Andre, your job is secure.
sentences.zh: 安德烈，你的工作很稳固。

sentences.en: Andre Walker first saw Oprah on her talk show, AM Chicago, back in the 80s.
sentences.zh: 安德烈·沃克第一次见到奥普拉是在80年代她的脱口秀节目《AM芝加哥》上。

sentences.en: I thought she was fantastic.
sentences.zh: 我觉得她太棒了。

sentences.en: And I was watching her show every morning.
sentences.zh: 我每天早上都在看她的节目。

sentences.en: And I thought, you know, I want to get to know her.
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道，我想认识她。

sentences.en: So I sent her some flowers one day saying, I'm dying to get my hands in your hair.
sentences.zh: 所以有一天我给她送了一些花，并写道：我渴望能亲手为你打理头发。

sentences.en: Please give me a call.
sentences.zh: 请给我打个电话。

sentences.en: He didn't have to do much convincing to get the job.
sentences.zh: 他没费什么口舌就得到了这份工作。

sentences.en: She called me the next day.
sentences.zh: 她第二天就给我打了电话。

sentences.en: And I'm thinking, oh my God, that was easy.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，天哪，这太容易了。

sentences.en: Andre traveled the globe with Oprah as she became one of the most important media figures in the world.
sentences.zh: 安德烈跟随奥普拉走遍全球，见证她成为世界上最重要的媒体人物之一。

sentences.en: And he gave her basically every hairstyle imaginable.
sentences.zh: 他几乎为她设计了你能想象到的所有发型。

sentences.en: Chin-length bob, very layered and spiky.
sentences.zh: 下巴长度的波波头，非常有层次感且带刺感。

sentences.en: That was one of my favorites, you know, flippy.
sentences.zh: 那是我的最爱之一，你知道，那种翻翘的效果。

sentences.en: We did a cover with an afro on her magazine with this huge afro wig that was very popular.
sentences.zh: 我们曾为她的杂志封面做过一个爆炸头造型，用的是当时非常流行的超大爆炸头假发。

sentences.en: God, I can go on and on and on.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我可以没完没了地说下去。

sentences.en: But beyond Oprah's hair, Andre's known for something else.
sentences.zh: 但除了奥普拉的头发，安德烈还因另一件事而闻名。

sentences.en: A system that he created back in the 90s to market his line of hair care products.
sentences.zh: 他在90年代为了推销他的护发产品系列而创建的一套系统。

sentences.en: The system categorizes natural hair types.
sentences.zh: 该系统对自然发质类型进行了分类。

sentences.en: And it's come to be known as the hair chart.
sentences.zh: 它后来被称为“发质图表”。

sentences.en: Andre Walker hair takes your natural where it's never gone before.
sentences.zh: 安德烈·沃克护发产品带你的自然发质去往从未到达过的地方。

sentences.en: The hair typing chart consists of four hair types.
sentences.zh: 发质分类图表包含四种发质类型。

sentences.en: Within each of those categories, there are different subtypes.
sentences.zh: 在每个类别中，还有不同的子类型。

sentences.en: Types 1 is for straight hair.
sentences.zh: 1型是直发。

sentences.en: Types 2 is for wavy hair.
sentences.zh: 2型是波浪发。

sentences.en: Types 3 is for curly hair.
sentences.zh: 3型是卷发。

sentences.en: And type 4 is for kinky hair.
sentences.zh: 4型是紧密卷曲发。

sentences.en: Go for the gold by Andre Walker.
sentences.zh: 安德烈·沃克助你追求极致。

sentences.en: For kinky, curly, and textured hair.
sentences.zh: 专为紧密卷曲、卷曲和纹理发质设计。

sentences.en: Andre's hair chart shows each type of hair drawn out and labeled.
sentences.zh: 安德烈的发质图表展示了每种发质的绘图和标签。

sentences.en: From bigger, loopy curls to super tight corkscrews.
sentences.zh: 从较大的环状卷发到超紧密的螺旋卷。

sentences.en: You can actually cut off a small piece of your hair and compare it to the drawings on the chart to figure out which one you are.
sentences.zh: 你实际上可以剪下一小撮头发，对照图表上的图画来确定你是哪一种。

sentences.en: I'm what's considered a 4B.
sentences.zh: 我属于4B型。

sentences.en: So I'm on the kinkier end of the curl spectrum.
sentences.zh: 所以我处于卷曲光谱中较紧密的那一端。

sentences.en: And for Andre, it was all about selling his products.
sentences.zh: 对安德烈来说，这一切都是为了销售他的产品。

sentences.en: If your hair is like this, you buy this product.
sentences.zh: 如果你的头发是这样的，你就买这个产品。

sentences.en: If it's like that, you buy this other one.
sentences.zh: 如果它是那样的，你就买另一个。

sentences.en: Your hair will feel so moist and touchable, you won't know what to do with yourself.
sentences.zh: 你的头发会感觉如此滋润、触感柔软，让你爱不释手。

sentences.en: I found Andre's chart after I decided to go natural.
sentences.zh: 我在决定回归自然发质后发现了安德烈的图表。

sentences.en: Like a lot of black women, I spent years putting chemical relaxers in my hair to straighten it.
sentences.zh: 像许多黑人女性一样，我花了很多年用化学柔顺剂来拉直头发。

sentences.en: It actually never even occurred to me not to relax my hair.
sentences.zh: 我甚至从未想过不去拉直头发。

sentences.en: Until I was living in Cuba, where relaxers were hard to come by.
sentences.zh: 直到我住在古巴，那里很难买到柔顺剂。

sentences.en: And so one day in Cuba, I just decided to do the big chop.
sentences.zh: 所以有一天在古巴，我决定进行“大剪”。

sentences.en: To cut my hair and let it grow back natural.
sentences.zh: 剪掉头发，让它自然长出来。

sentences.en: And it felt like a big deal.
sentences.zh: 这感觉像是一件大事。

sentences.en: For a while, I didn't even know how to manage it.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，我甚至不知道该如何打理它。

sentences.en: Sometimes I felt frumpy with my short, tight hair that I couldn't even comb through.
sentences.zh: 有时我觉得自己很邋遢，因为我的头发又短又紧，连梳子都梳不通。

sentences.en: I'd put on bright red lipstick and big hoop earrings.
sentences.zh: 我会涂上鲜红的口红，戴上大圆耳环。

sentences.en: Anything to get through what some people call the ugly phase.
sentences.zh: 想尽一切办法度过人们所说的“丑陋阶段”。

sentences.en: All of this was a big change.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是巨大的改变。

sentences.en: Not just the hair, but how people reacted to me.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是头发，还有人们对我的反应。

sentences.en: In Cuba, I went from being called mulata, which is more of a mixed girl, to negra, which is black girl.
sentences.zh: 在古巴，我从被称为“混血女孩”变成了“黑人女孩”。

sentences.en: Ay, you look negra now.
sentences.zh: 哎，你现在看起来像个黑人女孩了。

sentences.en: But somehow negra didn't feel like a compliment.
sentences.zh: 但不知为何，“黑人女孩”听起来并不像是一种赞美。

sentences.en: I felt pretty loSt.
sentences.zh: 我感到很迷茫。

sentences.en: So I turned to YouTube to find a community of other naturals.
sentences.zh: 所以我转向YouTube寻找其他自然发质人群的社区。

sentences.en: And there was Andre's system being referenced all over the place.
sentences.zh: 到处都能看到对安德烈系统的引用。

sentences.en: What is your hair type?
sentences.zh: 你的发质是什么类型的？

sentences.en: That has to be the, like, most frequently asked question.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是人们问得最多的问题。

sentences.en: 4C hair is a beautiful creation.
sentences.zh: 4C发质是一种美丽的创造。

sentences.en: You feel me?
sentences.zh: 你懂我的意思吗？

sentences.en: And it's most beautiful when you take care of her.
sentences.zh: 当你呵护它时，它是最美的。

sentences.en: The front portion of my hair is 3C.
sentences.zh: 我前额部分的头发是3C型的。

sentences.en: Andre's chart has gone way beyond his own line of hair care products.
sentences.zh: 安德烈的图表已经远远超出了他自己的护发产品系列。

sentences.en: It's become the go-to way for many of us to understand and talk about the texture of our hair.
sentences.zh: 它已成为我们许多人了解和谈论头发纹理的首选方式。

sentences.en: But not everyone thinks Andre's categories are a good thing.
sentences.zh: 但并非所有人都认为安德烈的分类是件好事。

sentences.en: In fact, I'm not sure they're a good thing.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我不确定它们是否是件好事。

sentences.en: But his chart has definitely got me thinking about the complicated relationship African Americans have with our hair.
sentences.zh: 但他的图表确实让我开始思考非裔美国人与头发之间复杂的关系。

sentences.en: It's a complicated relationship that goes way back.
sentences.zh: 这是一种由来已久的复杂关系。

sentences.en: Thick, kinky hair was considered a sign of health and wealth in parts of Africa.
sentences.zh: 在非洲部分地区，浓密、紧密的卷发被视为健康和财富的象征。

sentences.en: But in America, skin tone and hair texture was used to divide enslaved African people.
sentences.zh: 但在美国，肤色和发质被用来划分被奴役的非洲人。

sentences.en: Light skin and straighter hair could mean more privileges, like working in the house and not in the field.
sentences.zh: 肤色较浅、头发较直可能意味着更多的特权，比如在室内工作而不是在田间劳作。

sentences.en: This idea of good hair and bad hair all developed during slavery.
sentences.zh: 这种“好头发”和“坏头发”的观念都是在奴隶制时期形成的。

sentences.en: This idea that the straighter your hair was or the closer it was to white textured hair, the better it was.
sentences.zh: 这种观念认为，头发越直，或者越接近白人的发质，就越好。

sentences.en: Ayanna Byrd is the co-author of Hair Story, Untangling the Roots of Black Hair in America.
sentences.zh: 阿亚娜·伯德是《发之史：解开美国黑人头发的根源》一书的合著者。

sentences.en: And she says the common belief back then was...
sentences.zh: 她说当时普遍的看法是……

sentences.en: If you had straighter hair, you probably had more white blood than someone who didn't have straighter hair.
sentences.zh: 如果你头发较直，你可能比头发不直的人拥有更多的白人血统。

sentences.en: After slavery ended, these racist beauty standards hung on.
sentences.zh: 奴隶制结束后，这些种族主义的审美标准依然存在。

sentences.en: In the early 1900s, some people tried to straighten their hair by putting oil on it and then wrapping it with heated flannel.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪初，有些人试图通过涂油并用加热的法兰绒包裹来拉直头发。

sentences.en: Mothers were even wrapping their children's hair, often causing burns and a lot of hair damage.
sentences.zh: 母亲们甚至会包裹孩子们的头发，这经常导致烧伤和严重的头发损伤。

sentences.en: There were even black churches in certain cities that would hang a comb on the front door.
sentences.zh: 在某些城市的黑人教堂，甚至会在前门挂一把梳子。

sentences.en: And if you couldn't comb your hair with that, then you couldn't worship at that church.
sentences.zh: 如果你不能用那把梳子梳通头发，你就不能在那座教堂礼拜。

sentences.en: In the 1920s, hot combs were used to straighten hair.
sentences.zh: 20世纪20年代，热梳被用来拉直头发。

sentences.en: And then came a hairstyle known as the conch.
sentences.zh: 后来出现了一种被称为“康克”的发型。

sentences.en: You can see it on famous jazz musicians like Cab Calloway and Duke Ellington.
sentences.zh: 你可以在卡布·卡洛威和杜克·艾灵顿等著名的爵士音乐家身上看到它。

sentences.en: The conch was the name of the style, but it was also the name of the relaxer itself,
sentences.zh: “康克”是这种发型的名称，但它也是柔顺剂本身的名称，

sentences.en: which was made with a harsh chemical called sodium hydroxide.
sentences.zh: 它是由一种叫做氢氧化钠的强效化学物质制成的。

sentences.en: Or lye.
sentences.zh: 也就是碱液。

sentences.en: And it essentially just kind of ate away at your hair and at your scalp and caused a lot of serious burns.
sentences.zh: 它基本上会腐蚀你的头发和头皮，并导致许多严重的烧伤。

sentences.en: And they were not safe.
sentences.zh: 而且它们并不安全。

sentences.en: Some people made their own conchs.
sentences.zh: 有些人甚至自己制作“康克”柔顺剂。

sentences.en: Sometimes with two white potatoes, an egg, and red devil brand lye.
sentences.zh: 有时用两个白土豆、一个鸡蛋和红魔牌碱液。

sentences.en: A combo that left many scalps bleeding.
sentences.zh: 这种组合让许多人的头皮流血。

sentences.en: The conch eventually went out of style.
sentences.zh: “康克”最终退出了流行。

sentences.en: But relaxers made with sodium hydroxide continued on and became more and more popular.
sentences.zh: 但用氢氧化钠制成的柔顺剂却延续下来，并变得越来越受欢迎。

sentences.en: The wash and set and under the dryer with a magazine became a very common image in black salons.
sentences.zh: 洗发、定型，然后在烘干机下看杂志，成了黑人沙龙里非常常见的景象。

sentences.en: But then, in the 1960s, something different started rising.
sentences.zh: 但到了20世纪60年代，一些不同的东西开始兴起。

sentences.en: We have come to register to vote.
sentences.zh: 我们来这里是为了登记投票。

sentences.en: And you must realize that this is a national issue.
sentences.zh: 你们必须意识到这是一个全国性的问题。

sentences.en: It's not a Selma issue.
sentences.zh: 这不是塞尔玛的问题。

sentences.en: It's not an Alabama issue.
sentences.zh: 这不是阿拉巴马州的问题。

sentences.en: This is a national issue.
sentences.zh: 这是一个全国性的问题。

sentences.en: The civil rights movement brought on the beginning of a new shift that was all about embracing blackness.
sentences.zh: 民权运动带来了一个新的转变，其核心是拥抱黑人身份。

sentences.en: And this meant embracing your natural hair.
sentences.zh: 这意味着拥抱你自然的头发。

sentences.en: My mom, aunties, they all did the big chop.
sentences.zh: 我的妈妈、阿姨们，她们都进行了“大剪”。

sentences.en: Cutting out the relaxers and wearing their afros loud and proud.
sentences.zh: 剪掉柔顺剂，大声而自豪地展示她们的爆炸头。

sentences.en: This brother here, myself, all of us, were born with our hair like this.
sentences.zh: 这位兄弟，我自己，我们所有人，生来头发就是这样的。

sentences.en: And we just wear it like this.
sentences.zh: 我们只是这样留着它。

sentences.en: This is an interview from 1968 with former Black Panther Kathleen Cleaver.
sentences.zh: 这是一段1968年对前黑豹党成员凯瑟琳·克利弗的采访。

sentences.en: For so many, many years, we were told that only white people were beautiful.
sentences.zh: 多年来，我们被告知只有白人才是美丽的。

sentences.en: Only straight hair, light eyes, light skin was beautiful.
sentences.zh: 只有直发、浅色眼睛、浅色皮肤才是美丽的。

sentences.en: And so black women would try everything they could, straighten their hair, lighten their skin,
sentences.zh: 所以黑人女性会尝试一切可能的方法，拉直头发，美白皮肤，

sentences.en: to look as much like white women.
sentences.zh: 尽可能看起来像白人女性。

sentences.en: But this has changed because black people are aware.
sentences.zh: 但这已经改变了，因为黑人已经觉醒了。

sentences.en: And white people are aware of it, too, because white people now want natural wigs.
sentences.zh: 白人也意识到了这一点，因为白人现在也想要自然风格的假发。

sentences.en: They want wigs like this.
sentences.zh: 他们想要这样的假发。

sentences.en: Dig it?
sentences.zh: 懂了吗？

sentences.en: Isn't it beautiful?
sentences.zh: 它不美吗？

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Natural hair and afros were everywhere.
sentences.zh: 自然发型和爆炸头随处可见。

sentences.en: From the fluffy froes of the Jackson 5 to white celebrities like Barbra Streisand copying the fro.
sentences.zh: 从杰克逊五人组蓬松的爆炸头，到芭芭拉·史翠珊等白人名流模仿这种发型。

sentences.en: It was the first time that the relaxer industry, the chemical relaxer industry, was really taking a hit financially.
sentences.zh: 这是柔顺剂行业，即化学柔顺剂行业，在经济上首次遭受重创。

sentences.en: And not as many people were chemically straightening their hair.
sentences.zh: 不再有那么多人使用化学手段拉直头发了。

sentences.en: Instead of straighteners, for the first time, people were seeing products that were meant to complement their natural hair.
sentences.zh: 人们第一次看到的不再是拉直产品，而是旨在衬托他们自然发质的产品。

sentences.en: Like AfroSheen, which gave the afro a bit more shine and made it glisten like a halo in the sunlight.
sentences.zh: 就像AfroSheen，它能让爆炸头多一点光泽，在阳光下闪耀得如同光环一般。

sentences.en: AfroSheen!
sentences.zh: AfroSheen！

sentences.en: AfroSheen!
sentences.zh: AfroSheen！

sentences.en: Even as afros continued to be an important style, in the 1980s, a new chemical hairdo was on the rise.
sentences.zh: 尽管爆炸头依然是一种重要的发型，但到了20世纪80年代，一种新的化学处理发型开始兴起。

sentences.en: Sexy?
sentences.zh: 性感吗？

sentences.en: One, two, three.
sentences.zh: 一，二，三。

sentences.en: Just love yourself.
sentences.zh: 只要爱你自己就好。

sentences.en: The jerry curl created a bigger, looser curl pattern.
sentences.zh: 杰里卷（jerry curl）创造了一种更大、更松散的卷发纹理。

sentences.en: It was a turn away from the political statement of the afro.
sentences.zh: 这标志着人们开始背离爆炸头所代表的政治宣言。

sentences.en: The jerry curl was all about fun.
sentences.zh: 杰里卷主打的就是一个玩乐心态。

sentences.en: So the ads really shifted away from having anything to do with Black culture and community building and Black identity.
sentences.zh: 所以广告宣传的重点真的不再与黑人文化、社区建设和黑人身份认同有任何关联了。

sentences.en: And it's more to just, you know, neon colors and partying and like all of the advertising for jerry curls.
sentences.zh: 更多的是，你知道，霓虹色彩、派对狂欢，这就是杰里卷所有的广告风格。

sentences.en: More about this, like embracing this fun, easy to go style.
sentences.zh: 更多是关于拥抱这种有趣、易于打理的风格。

sentences.en: Although nothing about the jerry curl was easy.
sentences.zh: 尽管杰里卷一点也不好打理。

sentences.en: Jerry curls were the most product-heavy hairstyle that I think any people have ever known.
sentences.zh: 我认为杰里卷是任何人都见过最依赖护发产品的发型。

sentences.en: Black people, white people, doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 不管是黑人还是白人，都一样。

sentences.en: Like to have a jerry curl, you had to have all of that activator and so much stuff and you had to use it every single day.
sentences.zh: 想要留杰里卷，你必须用上所有的激活剂和各种各样的东西，而且每天都得用。

sentences.en: The jerry curl was a very moisturized style.
sentences.zh: 杰里卷是一种非常需要滋润的发型。

sentences.en: The activator that you had to put in your hair every day was drippy and greasy and your pillow would be stained with it.
sentences.zh: 你每天必须涂在头发上的激活剂又滴又油，你的枕头都会被弄脏。

sentences.en: Wearing a shower cap in public was quite normal.
sentences.zh: 在公共场合戴着浴帽是相当正常的。

sentences.en: I know all of this because when I was a kid, I had one.
sentences.zh: 我之所以知道这些，是因为我小时候也留过。

sentences.en: When the jerry curl faded out, regular old relaxers were still an option.
sentences.zh: 当杰里卷热潮退去后，普通的传统直发膏依然是一个选择。

sentences.en: And I went back to a relaxer too.
sentences.zh: 我也重新用回了直发膏。

sentences.en: Then, in 2009, comedian Chris Rock produced a documentary called Good Hair after his daughter asked him,
sentences.zh: 后来，在2009年，喜剧演员克里斯·洛克（Chris Rock）在女儿问他一个问题后，制作了一部名为《好头发》（Good Hair）的纪录片：

sentences.en: Daddy, how come I don't have good hair?
sentences.zh: 爸爸，为什么我没有好头发？

sentences.en: In the documentary, he refers to chemical relaxers as creamy crack because they're applied in a white paste.
sentences.zh: 在纪录片中，他把化学直发膏称为“奶油毒药”（creamy crack），因为它们涂抹时就像白色的膏状物。

sentences.en: And even though they're toxic, some people can't seem to quit them.
sentences.zh: 尽管它们有毒，但有些人似乎就是戒不掉。

sentences.en: In one scene, he shows just how harsh the chemicals found in many relaxers can be.
sentences.zh: 在其中一个场景中，他展示了许多直发膏中所含化学物质的严酷性。

sentences.en: He meets up with this chemist who demonstrates how sodium hydroxide can eat through just about anything.
sentences.zh: 他见了一位化学家，演示了氢氧化钠几乎可以腐蚀任何东西。

sentences.en: Sodium hydroxide will burn through your skin.
sentences.zh: 氢氧化钠会灼伤你的皮肤。

sentences.en: The chicken is your skin.
sentences.zh: 这块鸡肉就是你的皮肤。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So it'll go from my brown skin down to the white meat.
sentences.zh: 所以它会从我的棕色皮肤一直腐蚀到里面的白肉。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Now you realize this goes in people's heads, right?
sentences.zh: 现在你意识到这东西是涂在人头上的，对吧？

sentences.en: Sodium hydroxide?
sentences.zh: 氢氧化钠？

sentences.en: Yeah, people, black people, black women, some men, you know, Morris Day, Prince,
sentences.zh: 是的，人们，黑人，黑人女性，还有一些男性，你知道的，莫里斯·戴（Morris Day）、王子（Prince），

sentences.en: put sodium hydroxide in their hair to straighten it out.
sentences.zh: 他们把氢氧化钠涂在头发上以拉直头发。

sentences.en: Why would they do that?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么要那样做？

sentences.en: To look white.
sentences.zh: 为了看起来像白人。

sentences.en: That's what you talked about, you see, how some hair come in tighter than this.
sentences.zh: 这就是你刚才提到的，你看，有些头发天生就比这个更卷。

sentences.en: This is like a, maybe like a three, four.
sentences.zh: 这大概是三、四级的样子。

sentences.en: Feel it.
sentences.zh: 摸摸看。

sentences.en: Do you mind if she cut your hair?
sentences.zh: 你不介意她剪你的头发吧？

sentences.en: That's Annetta Dingle-Smith.
sentences.zh: 那是安内塔·丁格尔-史密斯（Annetta Dingle-Smith）。

sentences.en: And I'm with her in her salon in Boston, which amazingly is called Girlfriend Hooked Me Up Salon.
sentences.zh: 我和她在一起，在波士顿她的沙龙里，这家沙龙的名字非常惊人，叫“闺蜜帮我搞定沙龙”（Girlfriend Hooked Me Up Salon）。

sentences.en: Everybody was saying, girlfriend, you hooked me up.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在说，闺蜜，你帮我搞定了。

sentences.en: So that's how I came up with the name.
sentences.zh: 所以我才想出了这个名字。

sentences.en: Smith tells me that even though the Chris Rock movie brought up some deep-rooted stuff that we need to talk about,
sentences.zh: 史密斯告诉我，尽管克里斯·洛克的电影提出了一些我们需要讨论的根深蒂固的问题，

sentences.en: it also did actually affect her business.
sentences.zh: 但它确实影响了她的生意。

sentences.en: People used to come in every six to eight weeks to get relaxers.
sentences.zh: 人们过去每六到八周就会来做一次直发护理。

sentences.en: Some women would spend well over $1,000 a year on regular treatments in salons.
sentences.zh: 有些女性每年在沙龙的常规护理上花费超过1000美元。

sentences.en: Smith thinks the Chris Rock movie had an effect on all that.
sentences.zh: 史密斯认为克里斯·洛克的电影对这一切产生了影响。

sentences.en: For a minute, I was mad at the cause, you know.
sentences.zh: 有一阵子，我真的很生这部片子的气，你知道的。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Because it was affecting my money.
sentences.zh: 因为它影响了我的收入。

sentences.en: Everybody started going natural.
sentences.zh: 每个人都开始回归自然发质了。

sentences.en: You know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: So that did take an impact on me with me having chemical clients.
sentences.zh: 所以这对我那些做化学护理的客户确实产生了影响。

sentences.en: Because not everybody wanted to pour their hair out.
sentences.zh: 因为不是每个人都想把头发弄掉。

sentences.en: They don't want that creamy crack.
sentences.zh: 他们不想用那种“奶油毒药”。

sentences.en: Today, Black consumer spending on relaxers is down 30% since 2011.
sentences.zh: 如今，黑人消费者在直发膏上的支出自2011年以来下降了30%。

sentences.en: And this brings us back to Andre Walker's hair chart.
sentences.zh: 这又让我们回到了安德烈·沃克（Andre Walker）的头发分类表。

sentences.en: All of these newly natural people are getting on YouTube for advice and discovering the chart.
sentences.zh: 所有这些刚回归自然发质的人都在YouTube上寻求建议，并发现了这张表。

sentences.en: Unbeknownst to me, I was on the internet one day and I was reading some bloggers and they were referring to the Andre Walker hair typing system.
sentences.zh: 我当时完全不知情，有一天我在网上读一些博主的文章，他们提到了安德烈·沃克的头发分类系统。

sentences.en: I'm like, did I do that?
sentences.zh: 我在想，那是我做的吗？

sentences.en: Is that the one I wrote about in my book?
sentences.zh: 那是我在书里写的那一套吗？

sentences.en: These days, all over YouTube, there are people referencing Andre's chart.
sentences.zh: 这些天，在YouTube上到处都有人在引用安德烈的分类表。

sentences.en: Which, remember, categorizes hair from one to four.
sentences.zh: 记住，它将头发分为一到四类。

sentences.en: One A being looser curls and four C being the tightest curls.
sentences.zh: 1A是较松的卷发，4C是最紧的卷发。

sentences.en: So I'm just going to be braiding my hair so I can get my afro to be, like, rounded into the front.
sentences.zh: 所以我打算把头发编起来，这样我的爆炸头就能在前面呈现出圆润的形状。

sentences.en: There are videos on the best creams for a 4B twist out or how many times a week you should wash your 3B hair or lists of protective styles for your 4C hair.
sentences.zh: 网上有很多关于4B发质最适合什么护发霜的视频，或者关于你应该每周洗几次3B头发的建议，还有各种针对4C发质的保护性发型清单。

sentences.en: And at first I found this all really helpful and positive.
sentences.zh: 起初，我发现这一切非常有帮助且积极。

sentences.en: I mean, it's great that more people are going natural and it's great that there's a system to help them to do it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，更多人回归自然发质是件好事，而且有一个系统来帮助他们做到这一点也很棒。

sentences.en: But then a few people started noticing that even in this new online community of naturals,
sentences.zh: 但后来一些人开始注意到，即使在这个新的自然发质在线社区中，

sentences.en: a lot of the videos were just reinforcing old bias about straighter hair being better.
sentences.zh: 很多视频依然在强化那种“直发更好”的旧偏见。

sentences.en: The videos often instruct women about how to go from very kinky hair to less kinky, straighter hair.
sentences.zh: 这些视频经常指导女性如何从非常卷曲的头发变成卷度较小、更直的头发。

sentences.en: So, like, from a 4C to a 3B without using chemicals.
sentences.zh: 比如，在不使用化学品的情况下从4C变成3B。

sentences.en: But still implying that straighter is better.
sentences.zh: 但这依然暗示着“直发更好”。

sentences.en: You rarely see hair like this dominating hair campaigns, but you do see fluffy, bouncy, curly hair in all the hair campaigns.
sentences.zh: 你很少看到像这样的头发主导护发广告，但你确实在所有的护发广告中看到蓬松、有弹性、卷曲的头发。

sentences.en: There are people like myself with 4C hair that I literally cannot get my hand through it, so our problems are not the same.
sentences.zh: 像我这样拥有4C发质的人，手根本插不进头发里，所以我们的问题是不一样的。

sentences.en: We should be given room to speak.
sentences.zh: 我们应该有发言权。

sentences.en: That's a post from Slumflower, a popular blogger, who makes a lot of straight-talk, self-care types of videos.
sentences.zh: 那是Slumflower的一篇帖子，她是一位受欢迎的博主，制作了很多直言不讳、关于自我护理的视频。

sentences.en: People like ourselves do not have hair that grows downwards.
sentences.zh: 像我们这样的人，头发不是向下生长的。

sentences.en: Our hair grows upwards.
sentences.zh: 我们的头发是向上生长的。

sentences.en: Even if my hair is about...
sentences.zh: 即使我的头发大约……

sentences.en: It feels to Slumflower and others like online natural hair talk is mostly about how to transform what we have into something else.
sentences.zh: 对于Slumflower和其他人来说，网上的自然发质讨论大多是关于如何把我们现有的头发变成另一种样子。

sentences.en: Something a little looser.
sentences.zh: 变成一种稍微松散一点的样子。

sentences.en: That's not what our hair naturally does.
sentences.zh: 那不是我们头发自然生长的样子。

sentences.en: And they're using Andre's chart to do it.
sentences.zh: 而他们正在利用安德烈的分类表来达到这个目的。

sentences.en: There's been a lot of criticism against a lot of natural hair websites that they focus too much on quote-unquote 3B hair as opposed to 4C hair.
sentences.zh: 很多自然发质网站受到了批评，因为它们过于关注所谓的3B发质，而不是4C发质。

sentences.en: And that the tighter your curl pattern is and the kinkier your hair is, the less represented you are on these sites.
sentences.zh: 而且你的卷发纹理越紧、头发越卷，你在这些网站上的代表性就越低。

sentences.en: One woman I talked to said the chart feels to her like a modern-day pencil test, which was a test used in apartheid South Africa to figure out if someone was white or black.
sentences.zh: 我采访过的一位女性说，这张表对她来说就像现代版的“铅笔测试”，这曾是种族隔离时期的南非用来判断某人是白人还是黑人的测试。

sentences.en: If you put a pencil in someone's hair and the pencil fell out, the person passed and was considered white.
sentences.zh: 如果你把一支铅笔插进某人的头发里，如果铅笔掉下来，那个人就通过了测试，被认为是白人。

sentences.en: But Andre Walker says he just wanted to make a variety of products for different kinds of hair.
sentences.zh: 但安德烈·沃克说，他只是想为不同类型的头发制作各种各样的产品。

sentences.en: It wasn't at all his intention to create a hierarchy.
sentences.zh: 他根本没有建立等级制度的意图。

sentences.en: People have asked me why did I label straight hair as number one and kinky hair as number four.
sentences.zh: 人们问我为什么把直发标为第一类，把卷发标为第四类。

sentences.en: I also asked him.
sentences.zh: 我也问过他。

sentences.en: But my answer to that is it's going from zero texture to highly textured.
sentences.zh: 但我的回答是，这是从零纹理到高度纹理的过渡。

sentences.en: So going from one being straight to four being the kinkieSt.
sentences.zh: 所以从1号的直发到4号的最卷发。

sentences.en: And I've had people that have been very sensitive about that because they thought that I was giving kinky hair less importance by putting it in number four and giving straight hair more importance by being number one.
sentences.zh: 有些人对此非常敏感，因为他们认为我把卷发放在第四类是降低了它的重要性，而把直发放在第一类则是提高了它的重要性。

sentences.en: But that just goes to show you how sensitive, you know, hair is, hair and texture is, you know, for a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 但这恰恰说明了对很多人来说，头发和纹理是多么敏感的话题。

sentences.en: It's true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: It's so, so sensitive.
sentences.zh: 非常、非常敏感。

sentences.en: And even though a lot more women are going natural, there are still so many who just don't want to.
sentences.zh: 尽管越来越多的女性回归自然发质，但仍有许多人根本不想这样做。

sentences.en: Maybe they like the way their hair looks straightened or find it easier to manage or just don't want to deal with other people's reactions to their natural hair.
sentences.zh: 也许她们喜欢自己头发拉直后的样子，或者觉得那样更容易打理，又或者只是不想面对别人对她们自然发质的反应。

sentences.en: Back at Girlfriend Hooked Me Up Hair Salon, Yvette Moisa-Sunga says she isn't the least bit concerned with Andre's hair chart because she doesn't want to go natural.
sentences.zh: 回到“闺蜜帮我搞定沙龙”，伊薇特·莫伊萨-松加（Yvette Moisa-Sunga）说她一点也不关心安德烈的头发分类表，因为她不想回归自然发质。

sentences.en: Um, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不知道。

sentences.en: That look I feel is not for me.
sentences.zh: 我觉得那种造型不适合我。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: There's just this, should I say fear or discomfort?
sentences.zh: 这其中有一种，我该说是恐惧还是不适感？

sentences.en: You know, I'm not going to show up to an interview with braids on or fro or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我不会顶着编发或爆炸头去参加面试之类的。

sentences.en: It's, my hair is going to be as straight as it possibly can be because as much as I like it or don't like it,
sentences.zh: 我的头发必须尽可能地直，因为无论我喜不喜欢，

sentences.en: we still live in a society where our hair is not accepted for what it is.
sentences.zh: 我们依然生活在一个头发不被接受其本来面目的社会里。

sentences.en: And you have to play the game to win it.
sentences.zh: 你必须按规则行事才能赢。

sentences.en: There is so much racism and colorism and years of painful history tangled up in all of this.
sentences.zh: 这一切中纠缠着太多的种族主义、肤色歧视以及多年来痛苦的历史。

sentences.en: It's deeply personal.
sentences.zh: 这是非常私人的。

sentences.en: And for those of us who have decided to go natural,
sentences.zh: 对于我们这些决定回归自然发质的人来说，

sentences.en: it would be nice to see the hair conversation shift away from how to change our hair and more towards how to manage the natural texture we were born with.
sentences.zh: 如果关于头发的讨论能从“如何改变我们的头发”转向“如何打理我们天生的自然纹理”，那该多好。

sentences.en: Because my hair is still a crown, no matter where on the chart I land.
sentences.zh: 因为无论我在分类表上处于哪个位置，我的头发依然是我的皇冠。

sentences.en: Lila Day decodes the proud lady symbol for us right after this.
sentences.zh: 莉拉·戴（Lila Day）将在稍后为我们解读“骄傲女士”标志。

sentences.en: So one of the things we love to do on our show is decode little symbols that you see out in the design world.
sentences.zh: 我们在节目中喜欢做的一件事就是解读你在设计界看到的各种小标志。

sentences.en: And you're here to tell us about the proud lady symbol.
sentences.zh: 你今天来是为了告诉我们关于“骄傲女士”标志的事。

sentences.en: What is the proud lady symbol?
sentences.zh: 什么是“骄傲女士”标志？

sentences.en: So the proud lady symbol is the symbol of this black woman with these long locks behind her and her head is held proud.
sentences.zh: “骄傲女士”标志是一个黑人女性的符号，她身后有长长的发辫，头高高地昂着，充满自豪。

sentences.en: And you can see the symbol on the back of some hair care products.
sentences.zh: 你可以在一些护发产品的背面看到这个标志。

sentences.en: Oh, cool.
sentences.zh: 哦，酷。

sentences.en: And I actually grew up seeing the symbol everywhere.
sentences.zh: 我从小到大到处都能看到这个标志。

sentences.en: I just thought it was part of, you know, all the brands.
sentences.zh: 我一直以为它是所有品牌的一部分，你知道的。

sentences.en: But it's actually not.
sentences.zh: 但其实并不是。

sentences.en: It has a very specific point.
sentences.zh: 它有一个非常具体的意义。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: What's the point?
sentences.zh: 是什么意义？

sentences.en: There was an organization called the American Health and Beauty AIDS Institute.
sentences.zh: 有一个组织叫“美国健康与美容艾滋病协会”（American Health and Beauty AIDS Institute）。

sentences.en: And they were founded in the 80s after a lot of black hair care products were kind of getting lost in the consumer market.
sentences.zh: 他们成立于80年代，当时很多黑人护发产品在消费市场上快要被淹没了。

sentences.en: There were big corporations like Revlon and Johnson & Johnson.
sentences.zh: 当时有像露华浓（Revlon）和强生（Johnson & Johnson）这样的大公司。

sentences.en: And they were sort of taking over the black hair care business.
sentences.zh: 它们几乎接管了黑人护发业务。

sentences.en: So they created the proud lady symbol to let people know that it's a black-owned business.
sentences.zh: 所以他们创造了“骄傲女士”标志，让人们知道这是黑人拥有的企业。

sentences.en: Oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 哦，好的。

sentences.en: So what do you have in your hand there?
sentences.zh: 那你手里拿的是什么？

sentences.en: So I'm holding some Luster's pink therapeutic conditioning hairdress.
sentences.zh: 我手里拿的是Luster's的粉色治疗性护发素。

sentences.en: I haven't used it yet.
sentences.zh: 我还没用过。

sentences.en: I used to use Luster's when I was a kid.
sentences.zh: 我小时候用过Luster's的产品。

sentences.en: But there's the proud lady symbol right on the back near the barcode.
sentences.zh: 看，背面条形码附近就有“骄傲女士”标志。

sentences.en: And, yeah, it says in really tiny little writing.
sentences.zh: 而且，是的，上面写着非常小的字。

sentences.en: Let me see if I can see.
sentences.zh: 让我看看能不能看清。

sentences.en: It says the proud lady, 100% black-owned.
sentences.zh: 上面写着“骄傲女士，100%黑人拥有”。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That's great.
sentences.zh: 那太棒了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So to this day, do you look for that and make your choices based on that?
sentences.zh: 所以直到今天，你还会寻找那个标志并以此作为选择的依据吗？

sentences.en: I never have, you know.
sentences.zh: 我从来没有过，你知道的。

sentences.en: And it was just doing this piece that I was like, oh, that symbol.
sentences.zh: 只是在做这一期节目的时候，我突然想到，哦，那个标志。

sentences.en: I grew up seeing that symbol.
sentences.zh: 我从小到大一直都能看到那个标志。

sentences.en: So I went to the hair care store and I looked for it over and over and over and over again.
sentences.zh: 所以我去了美发用品店，一遍又一遍地寻找它。

sentences.en: And I only saw it on a couple of products, you know.
sentences.zh: 但我只在少数几种产品上看到了它，你知道的。

sentences.en: So I don't know if it's obviously not used as much as it used to be.
sentences.zh: 所以我不知道，显然它不像过去用得那么多了。

sentences.en: But I kind of miss seeing that symbol.
sentences.zh: 但我有点怀念看到那个标志的感觉。

sentences.en: So if you want to make informed choices, look for the proud lady symbol.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想做出明智的选择，就去寻找那个“骄傲女士”的标志吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, look for her.
sentences.zh: 没错，找她就对了。

sentences.en: She looks proud.
sentences.zh: 她看起来很骄傲。

sentences.en: She does.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Thanks so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 不客气。

sentences.en: The Stoop Podcast is stories from across the black diaspora, hosted by Lila Day and Hanat Bamba.
sentences.zh: 《The Stoop》播客讲述的是来自全球黑人侨民的故事，由莱拉·戴和哈纳特·班巴主持。

sentences.en: It's conversations about blackness that aren't talked about enough, like is it appropriation
sentences.zh: 节目探讨了那些讨论不足的黑人议题，比如这算不算文化挪用：

sentences.en: when African-Americans wear African clothing or what it means when people say you sound white.
sentences.zh: 非裔美国人穿非洲传统服饰，或者当人们说你“听起来像个白人”时意味着什么。

sentences.en: You can subscribe to The Stoop wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 你可以在任何收听播客的平台上订阅《The Stoop》。

sentences.en: We're on Instagram, Tumblr, and Reddit too.
sentences.zh: 我们也在 Instagram、Tumblr 和 Reddit 上活跃。

sentences.en: But our true home on the internet is 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 但我们在互联网上真正的家是 99pi.org。
